en.name: Stanislaus Kostka
en.summary: Polish nobleman's son who walked hundreds of miles on foot to join the Jesuits against his family's fierce opposition, and died as a young novice.
en.body: Stanislaus Kostka was sent from Poland to study in Vienna as a teenager and there felt a strong call to join the Society of Jesus, a decision his father, an influential nobleman, refused to permit, going so far as to have him physically prevented and threatened when local Jesuits likewise declined to admit him without parental consent for fear of the family's anger. Undeterred, Stanislaus walked roughly 350 miles, largely on foot and partly disguised as a beggar, to Germany, where a sympathetic Jesuit provincial finally admitted him, and from there he continued to Rome to begin his novitiate. He reported visions of the Virgin Mary and a strong premonition that he would die soon after arriving in Rome, which came true within less than a year when he died of a sudden fever in 1568, at only seventeen, having been a Jesuit novice for less than a year. He was canonized in 1726 alongside Aloysius Gonzaga.
